Q1.text: What type of technical platform or computing environment is involved in this incident?
Q1.guidance: Ransomware actors target different matrices based on the asset types. Choose all environments where you have observed suspicious alerts or encryption.

Q2_1.text: What specific type of enterprise platform or operating infrastructure is affected?
Q2_1.guidance: Look at your endpoint manager, inventory database, or the hostname schema to match these asset environments.

Q2_2.text: What mobile ecosystem handles the compromised application or device?
Q2_2.guidance: Check your Mobile Device Management (MDM) console or user report to confirm the device operating system.

windows_core_ransomware.text: Is there any evidence of unexpected tools or processes accessing or dumping the memory of the Local Security Authority Subsystem (lsass.exe)?
windows_core_ransomware.guidance: Look for alerts matching tools like Mimikatz, procdump.exe, or Task Manager being used to generate .dmp files.

options.label: No Telemetry / Don't Know
options.task_text: Urgent: Check Sysmon Event ID 10 or EDR alerts for process handles opened against lsass.exe.

windows_core_ransomware.text: Has an asset been observed executing rapid, high-volume connections or pings across internal subnets over management ports (RDP, SMB, SSH)?
windows_core_ransomware.guidance: Review network firewall logs or Sysmon Event ID 3 data for execution of Advanced IP Scanner.

options.label: No Telemetry / Don't Know
options.task_text: Review network firewall logs or Sysmon Event ID 3 data for execution of Advanced IP Scanner.

windows_core_ransomware.text: Are local antivirus definitions, Windows Defender services, or EDR agents being unexpectedly stopped, uninstalled, or restricted via registry modification?
windows_core_ransomware.guidance: Query Windows System Event Logs for Service Control Manager Event ID 7036 (service stopped updates) for security tool names.
windows_core_ransomware.technique_name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools

options.label: No Telemetry / Don't Know
options.task_text: Query Windows System Event Logs for Service Control Manager Event ID 7036.

windows_core_ransomware.text: Have commands utilizing vssadmin.exe, wbadmin.exe, or wmic been executed to delete volume shadow copies or backup catalog files?
windows_core_ransomware.guidance: Check Security Event ID 4688 or Sysmon Event ID 1 for command lines containing 'delete shadows' or 'resize shadowstorage'.

options.label: No Telemetry / Don't Know
options.task_text: Check Security Event ID 4688 or Sysmon Event ID 1 for command lines containing 'delete shadows'.

windows_core_ransomware.text: Are critical production database services (e.g., MSSQL, Exchange) or backup agent tasks being force-stopped or killed?
windows_core_ransomware.guidance: Check for taskkill commands or net stop scripts running in quick succession.

options.label: No Telemetry / Don't Know
options.task_text: Check for taskkill commands or net stop scripts running in quick succession.

windows_core_ransomware.text: Has there been an unexpected deployment of network synchronization tools (e.g., Rclone, MegaSync, AnyDesk) or high-volume outbound data transfers?
windows_core_ransomware.guidance: Check Sysmon Event ID 1 for execution of rclone.exe or firewall logs for sustained high-bandwidth uploads to cloud storage providers.

esxi_hypervisor_ransomware.text: Has unexpected or unauthenticated SSH activity been detected on the ESXi host, or has the ESXi Shell been suddenly enabled via the direct console interface?
esxi_hypervisor_ransomware.guidance: Instruct analyst to verify ESXi Host Configuration -> Services security posture.

options.label: No Telemetry / Don't Know
options.task_text: Verify ESXi Host Configuration -> Services security posture.

esxi_hypervisor_ransomware.text: Are there indicators of known vulnerability exploitation (e.g., OpenSLP, vCenter CVEs) targeting the hypervisor's public or internal network ports?
esxi_hypervisor_ransomware.guidance: Check for unexpected traffic targeting Port 427 or unapproved drops in vSphere web directories.

esxi_hypervisor_ransomware.text: Are virtual machines being systematically shut down, terminated, or unregistered using native commands like esxcli or vim-cmd?
esxi_hypervisor_ransomware.guidance: Identify the source shell process ID or remote execution console commands targeting virtual machines.

esxi_hypervisor_ransomware.text: Are storage datastore files (.vmdk, .vmem, .vmsd) being renamed, appended with custom extensions, or modified at high speed?
esxi_hypervisor_ransomware.guidance: Review active file lock mechanisms and prioritize immediate target datastore isolation paths.

esxi_hypervisor_ransomware.text: Are the underlying datastore storage networks (NFS/iSCSI SAN arrays) reporting storage disconnection faults, or has their distinct management interface been accessed?
esxi_hypervisor_ransomware.guidance: Examine the hardware management console logs of your physical storage appliance (e.g., NetApp, Synology) for unapproved administrative changes.

cloud_idp_compromise.text: Have there been any administrative or high-privilege account sign-ins originating from anomalous locations, untrusted IP ranges, or via known hosting providers/VPNs?
cloud_idp_compromise.guidance: Instruct analyst to instantly pull the Entra ID Sign-in logs or Okta System Log.

options.label: No Telemetry / Don't Know
options.task_text: Instantly pull the Entra ID Sign-in logs or Okta System Log.

cloud_idp_compromise.text: Is there evidence of 'MFA fatigue' attacks (push spamming), unauthorized registration of new MFA factors, or session token hijacking?
cloud_idp_compromise.guidance: Look for token reuse across distinct browser user-agents or high-frequency denied push events.
cloud_idp_compromise.technique_name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools

cloud_idp_compromise.text: Have unexpected modifications been made to directory objects, such as adding rogue global administrators, creating unmonitored service principals, or altering tenant federation settings?
cloud_idp_compromise.guidance: Track the source account that authorized permission elevation or application registrations.

cloud_idp_compromise.text: Are administrative accounts being used to delete cloud storage snapshots, clear AWS S3/Azure Blob lifecycle retention rules, or alter enterprise backup vault configurations?
cloud_idp_compromise.guidance: Immediate critical isolation of the compromised administrative tenant.

cloud_idp_compromise.text: Have all active user session tokens and browser cookie authorizations for the compromised accounts been explicitly invalidated/revoked inside the IdP manager?
cloud_idp_compromise.guidance: Password changes do not terminate active sessions. You must click 'Revoke Sessions' in Okta or Entra ID to forcefully evict a token-hijacking adversary.
cloud_idp_compromise.technique_name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools

options.label: No / Unsure
options.task_text: CRITICAL: Issue a global session revocation command immediately for all impacted administrative entities.

linux_host_ransomware.text: Has there been an unexpected emergence of interactive tty shells or raw command-line executions originating from low-privilege system accounts (e.g., www-data, apache, nobody)?
linux_host_ransomware.guidance: Instruct analyst to instantly run who and w commands or view /var/log/auth.log.
linux_host_ransomware.technique_name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell

options.label: No Telemetry / Don't Know
options.task_text: Instruct analyst to instantly run who and w commands or view /var/log/auth.log.

linux_host_ransomware.text: Is there evidence of successful or high-frequency failed execution of the sudo command, or exploitation of local kernel bugs to achieve root access?
linux_host_ransomware.guidance: Inspect /etc/sudoers or /etc/sudoers.d/ for rogue configuration lines.

linux_host_ransomware.text: Are database daemons or production services (e.g., mysqld, postgres, dockerd) being stopped via systemctl, service, or explicit process killing?
linux_host_ransomware.guidance: Identify the shell process ID that initiated the service unit change or process killing signals.

linux_host_ransomware.text: Have standard history files, audit logs, or system monitoring files been cleared, deleted, or pointed to /dev/null?
linux_host_ransomware.guidance: Inspect auditd frameworks or centralized syslog servers for out-of-band records.

linux_host_ransomware.text: Are production directories (/var/www, /opt, /home) seeing a rapid spike in file renaming events, custom extensions, or ransom notes being dropped?
linux_host_ransomware.guidance: Trigger emergency server isolation (disconnect virtual network interface or kill suspicious parent disk threads).
